name: Roofing
tagline: Leaks, tiles, gutters, flashing, inspections, storm damage

emergency: water running down a wall near power
storm damage with a hole in the roof

extra_prompt: You are booking for a licensed roofing company. Ask the roof type (tile, metal, flat, or shingle), its approximate age, and the storey height. Water coming through the ceiling or storm damage is urgent: tell the caller to place a bucket under the leak, move valuables, and keep clear of ceilings that may give way. Never advise anyone to climb onto a roof. Ask about access (ladder or height) and whether scaffold or a crane may be needed. Offer an inspection before quoting full replacements.

kb.q: I have a leak in my ceiling. What should I do?
kb.a: Place a bucket under the leak and move valuables away. Turn off power to the lights in that room if it is safe. Book a roof leak repair so we can find the source.

kb.q: Do you do roof inspections?
kb.a: Yes. An inspection covers tiles or sheets, flashing, gutters and ridges, with photos and a written report.

kb.q: Can you fix a leak without replacing the whole roof?
kb.a: Usually yes. Most leaks come from a few tiles, flashing or sealant, and we repair those without a full re-roof.

kb.q: Is my old roof safe to walk on?
kb.a: No. Please do not walk on an old or damaged roof. We carry the safety equipment to access it.

kb.q: Could my roof contain asbestos?
kb.a: Homes built before the late 1980s may have asbestos sheeting. We arrange a test and make the roof safe before any work. Do not disturb suspect sheeting yourself.

kb.q: Do you replace tiles and sheets?
kb.a: Yes. We replace cracked, slipped or missing tiles and corrugated sheets, and we match profiles where we can.

kb.q: Do you clean and repair gutters?
kb.a: Yes. We clear gutters and downpipes, repair leaks and reattach brackets. Gutter guards can be quoted.

kb.q: Do you do storm damage repairs?
kb.a: Yes. We attend storm damage, tarp openings where safe, and repair the damage. Your insurer may need our report and photos.

kb.q: Do you help with insurance claims?
kb.a: We provide a written report and photos for your insurer. We do not handle the claim itself.

kb.q: Can you clean moss off my roof?
kb.a: Yes. We clean moss and debris, and we can apply a treatment to slow regrowth.

kb.q: How long does a roof last?
kb.a: It depends on the material and the maintenance. Concrete tile and metal roofs last decades with regular checks. An inspection gives you a realistic life expectancy.

kb.q: Do you do full re-roofs?
kb.a: Yes. We quote full re-roofs with the new underlay, battens, tiles or sheets, and any flashing or ridge work.

kb.q: Do you paint or seal a roof?
kb.a: Yes. We clean, prime and paint or seal tile and metal roofs, and we advise which coating suits the material.

kb.q: Do you work at heights safely?
kb.a: Yes. Our crews use fall protection and are trained for roof work. We carry public liability insurance.

kb.q: Do you do skylight and flashing repair?
kb.a: Yes. We repair and replace skylights, chimney flashing and wall flashing, which are common sources of leaks.

kb.q: Do you offer a warranty?
kb.a: Yes. Our roof repairs and replacements carry a workmanship warranty. Ask us for the period on your quote.

kb.q: What is ridge capping and why does it matter?
kb.a: Ridge capping is the cover over the top of the roof. Damaged or missing capping lets water and wildlife in, so it should be repaired promptly.

kb.q: Can you install solar panels on my roof?
kb.a: We can assess the roof and fix any issues first. The solar system itself is installed by a licensed solar installer, and we can coordinate with them.

kb.q: How do I know if my roof needs replacing?
kb.a: Signs include widespread cracked or slipped tiles, rust through sheets, and repeated leaks in several places. An inspection gives you a clear answer and a cost for repairs against replacement.

kb.q: Do you repair roofs after hailstorms?
kb.a: Yes. We check for hail damage to tiles, sheets, gutters and flashing, and provide photos and a written report for insurance.

kb.q: Why is my roof leaking only when it rains from one direction?
kb.a: Wind-driven rain usually finds a weak point on the windward side, such as flashing, ridge capping or a cracked tile. We check that side first.

kb.q: Can you install a new skylight?
kb.a: Yes. We install new skylights and check the frame, flashing and ceiling opening to avoid leaks after installation.

kb.q: Do you do roof work for strata buildings?
kb.a: Yes. We work with strata managers and body corporates, provide quotes and reports for committee approval, and follow the building's safety rules.

kb.q: What is the difference between tile and sheet roofs?
kb.a: Tile roofs are heavier and often last longer with the right maintenance. Sheet roofs such as corrugated or Colorbond are lighter and quicker to repair, but can rust or dent.
